name: The Library With Two Todays
premise:
A library terminal says a book was borrowed today and returned tomorrow. The
librarian is about to archive the transaction, making both dates official.

objective.description: Reconcile the conflicting date records before checkout finalizes.

anchors.name: calendar_habit
anchors.description: Your trust that dates move in one direction.

terminal.observe_text:
The public display shows borrowed today, returned tomorrow. Patching it
would hide the contradiction only on this screen.

checkout_ledger.observe_text:
The source checkout record has both dates attached to one transaction.
Repair this before the archive copies it.

archive_queue.observe_text: The transaction is queued for archival. Delaying the queue buys a turn.

librarian.observe_text:
The librarian is about to approve the archive. A distraction helps timing,
not consistency.

transaction_history.observe_text:
The transaction history points back to one source ledger row. Audit can
confirm whether the display or the source is wrong.

today.scene_message: The source row collapses to one ordinary date. The display and archive agree a moment later.
today.system_note: Source record repair before downstream commitment.
today.discovered_rule: Edit source records before displays or archives copy the contradiction.

today.scene_message: The terminal now shows only today's date. The archive queue still holds tomorrow.

hold.scene_message: The archive job stalls on a routine lock. You have a little more time.

distract.scene_message: The librarian turns to answer a patron. The record is still split.

audit_entries.text:
Audit confirms one source row is split. The terminal is only repeating the
ledger; patch the checkout ledger before the archive copies it.

date_conflict.text:
The display is downstream. The checkout ledger is the lowest source record
and should be patched before archival.

scene_progression.message: The librarian approves the archive. Tomorrow is now filed under today.

hidden_rules: Information edits are cheapest at the source before observers commit copies.
Display fixes can be correct-looking and still incomplete.
